title: Sugarlang Exponents
description: The phrases that perform each competency in one language. HAND-AUTHORED -- this is the only per-language file a person writes by hand, and the competency inventory is generated from it plus the language-neutral curriculum. Structure only: whether a phrase's words resolve, and whether the competency exists, are checked by the build and reported in its failure list.

lang.description: BCP-47 code. Must match the directory this file sits in.

exponents.description: Keyed by competencyId. A competency absent here is simply not taught in this language yet, which is a legitimate state -- a language is authored one lesson at a time.

additionalProperties.description: The exponents for one competency. Each entry is ONE learner card, so the split between entries is the decision about what counts as one thing to know.

wordings.description: Ways of saying the same thing. Grouped here they are one card; separate entries are separate cards. The first is canonical and gives the exponent its id.

phrase.description: The target-language phrase, written correctly, accents and all. Lowercase unless the word itself takes a capital, and no TRAILING punctuation -- a semicolon joining two clauses mid-phrase is fine and B2 uses them. Unaccented spellings are DERIVED -- writing them here duplicates what the build already produces.

gloss.description: What this wording MEANS, per support language. Authored because it cannot be derived: `por favor` from its own words comes out `for favour`. Translate the phrase, do not describe the act.

lemmas.description: Pins a word in THIS phrase to the lemma it means. Only where the index resolves it the WRONG way -- Italian `sei` is the numeral before it is `essere`. A word that does not resolve at all needs a dictionary entry, not an override.
